Title: Police hunt parolee missing since Sept 15
Article:
KULAI: Police are looking for a 30-year-old parolee who has left the Johor Baru parole district without permission since Sept 15.
Kulai police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received a report on the man's disappearance on Sept 17.
"The man has been identified as Hari Raj Suresh, 30, with his last known address at Jalan Desa 2, Taman Desa Kulai.
"He weighs around 60kg and has a round face, flat nose, bald head and dark complexion," he said in a statement.
Tan said the report was lodged by a prison officer after the man could not be traced in Kulai and Johor Baru by the Johor Baru parole officer.
"The had not returned or been traced until the report was lodged.
"The complainant also tried to locate him at several places but was unsuccessful," he said.
Tan said the man was subsequently listed as wanted.
He urged anyone with information on the man or who knows his whereabouts to contact Kulai police station chief Inspector Abdul Mustafa Kamal Md Said or the Kulai district police headquarters control centre at 07-663 2222.

Title: 'Disclose your own record': Ex-PJ MP Lee hits back at PKR leader in MBPJ dispute
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has challenged PKR deputy secretary-general Bryan Ng to disclose his own attendance and voting record at Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) meetings, after being criticised over his participation in council discussions.
Lee said an MP was not an MBPJ member but could be invited to attend council meetings as an observer, without voting rights or the authority to approve council papers.
He said Ng, an MBPJ councillor, had focused on his attendance at council meetings instead of the policy issues he had raised.
"My primary arena is the Dewan Rakyat, parliamentary committees and engagement with ministries. That is where the voice of Petaling Jaya is carried to the federal level," he said in a statement today.
Lee said this differed from the role of a city councillor, who is appointed to sit on the council, scrutinise and debate matters before it, and vote on them.
He challenged Ng to disclose his attendance at MBPJ and committee meetings, as well as his position and voting record on the proposed Petaling Jaya Dispersal Link (PJD Link).
Lee also asked whether MBPJ had approved or signed an agreement for the Selangor Intelligent Parking scheme and, if so, whether Ng had objected or recorded his dissent.
He further challenged Ng to state PKR's official position on the two projects and calls for a royal commission of inquiry into what he described as the "corporate mafia".
Lee said his own position was public, including his opposition to the parking scheme and his call for the PJD Link concession to be terminated.
"The people of Petaling Jaya, and PKR's own members, deserve answers. If the party has a clear position, state it. If it does not, then the problem is not that I spoke up. The problem is that the party has stayed silent," he said.
He added that attending meetings meant little if problematic projects were allowed to proceed without objection.
Ng had
earlier criticised Lee
for allegedly failing to attend most meetings on the Petaling Jaya local plan despite being invited as the MP.
He said the plan was important in determining urban development, including land use, traffic, public facilities and the city's future planning.
Lee, a one-term MP, announced earlier today that
he was stepping down
as the Petaling Jaya MP following his 3-year suspension from PKR.
He plans to resign from the party on Monday.

Title: Selangor Sultan tells political leaders: No fighting, focus on people
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today met and dined with three of the state's Menteri Besar — two former office holders, Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo and Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, and incumbent Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The special meeting took place after a Yasin recitation, tahlil and prayers for safety held in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of His Royal Highness' 25th year of reign at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque here.
"This meeting reflects the Sultan of Selangor's continuous concern regarding the state's direction and the people's livelihood, whilst demonstrating the good relationship between the royal institution and the state's administrative leadership, including those who previously shouldered the responsibility," according to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page.
According to the post, Sultan Sharafuddin advised political leaders not to fight, squabble or wrestle for power to the point of triggering division among themselves.
Instead, he wanted all efforts and attention to be focused on the state's development, the well-being of the people, and the welfare of those in need.
Sultan Sharafuddin also said differences in stance and political ideologies should not be a barrier to cooperation for the benefit of the state and its people.
"Leadership responsibilities must be carried out with full trustworthiness, prioritising the people's interests above personal or political group interests.
"His Royal Highness also reminded that Selangor's progress must be accompanied by societal harmony and administrative stability.
"Hence, leaders must maintain an attitude of mutual respect and prioritise constructive discussions in addressing any differences," the post stated.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar provides RM2,000 aid to Tambun crash victims' family
Article:
IPOH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today provided RM2,000 in initial assistance to the family of three siblings involved in a road accident in Tambun that claimed the lives of two of them and left another seriously injured.
The contribution was handed over by Tambun Parliamentary Community Service Centre officer Muhammad Izzudin Hariz Bohari on behalf of Anwar, who is also the Tambun member of parliament.
Tambun Parliamentary Community Service Centre officer Ashraf Kahasani said Anwar had instructed the centre to provide the initial assistance to the family.
"The Prime Minister also conveyed his condolences to the victims' family and asked us to provide the assistance directly to the next of kin to help ease their burden.
"If further assistance is needed for the other victim who was injured and is currently being treated in hospital, we will look into how we can help," he said when met by reporters after the contribution was presented at the victim's family home in Taman Bagus, Tambun, here.
The accident, which occurred around 7.20am today, claimed the lives of a 19-year-old girl who was riding a Yamaha EZ115 and her nine-year-old sister.
Another sibling, aged 12, who was also riding pillion, sustained serious injuries and is receiving treatment at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital.
The victims' eldest sister, Nurul Aeina Ibrahim, 28, said she learnt about the accident involving her three siblings from their school teacher around 8am.
She said, however, that she was only informed of the accident and was not told that her sisters had died.
"It was only when I reached the scene that I was told they were gone," she said.
Nurul Aeina said Norhayati Qaliesha, who survived the incident, had yet to be told about her two sisters' deaths as she remained in critical condition.
The two victims killed in the crash, Elyana Nasuha and her younger sister Suhaila, were buried in a single grave at the Tambun Muslim Cemetery here around 6.30 pm.
Meanwhile, Perak Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPk) chief executive officer Syamsul Hazeman Md Salleh said MAIPk would bear the cost of the funeral arrangements for the two siblings.
He said the council would also provide necessary assistance to their surviving sister, who was seriously injured in the crash.
"MAIPk provides funeral management assistance for families who are unable to afford the costs, as well as for deceased persons without next of kin," he said in a statement.

Title: Police seek motivational speaker over alleged child sexual harassment, 'sugar baby' claims
Article:
KANGAR: Police have asked a freelance speaker to come forward to assist investigations into an alleged child sexual harassment case.
Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said police confirmed receiving a report concerning the incident involving the speaker at 2.09am on Sept 26.
He said the man who is also an independent preacher had been asked to appear at the Padang Besar district police headquarters.
"Police also urge any other victims who may have been involved with the motivational speaker to come forward and lodge a report to assist investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017," he said in a statement.
Hamzah said if convicted, the offender could face up to five years in prison and whipping.
"Members of the public or victims with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Sharifah Nur Fasihah Syed Sofian, at 04-9490824 or 019-8151602," he said.
Earlier, it was reported that a victim, who wished to be known as Sofia, 19, said she was introduced to the man after he watched her TikTok livestream, after which they exchanged messages on WhatsApp.
The married man allegedly approached victims through social media under the pretext of work or study matters before allegedly asking them to become "sugar babies" and engaging in indecent acts.
Meanwhile, another victim, Diana, 27, said she initially contacted the man for a collaboration involving a motivational programme.
However, she said the work-related relationship turned disturbing when the speaker, whom she believed was single, allegedly asked her to check into a hotel with him and have sex.
On Wednesday, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek directed all school programmes involving him to be
stopped immediately
to allow for a full investigation.

Title: Saravanan questions why 12-year-old son was brought to MACC HQ
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan questioned why the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) did not clarify that his 12-year-old son was not required to attend its headquarters before he brought him there on Monday.
In a Facebook post today, Saravanan said they were only informed after entering the premises that his son was not required to sign anything and could return home.
"If he did not need to be there, why was this not clarified before a 12-year-old was brought to an anti-corruption headquarters?" he wrote.
Earlier,
Saravanan criticised the agency's explanation,
describing it as "entirely illogical" for his 12-year-old son to appear at its headquarters.
"With one child abroad, it was reasonable to understand that the other was my 12-year-old son," he said.
Saravanan said he had already informed MACC officers that his son was a minor and had no property in his name.
"Yet it was only after he walked through the doors of MACC headquarters that we were told he did not need to sign anything and could go home," he said.
He said MACC had since claimed that his son was never meant to be served and suggested that the family might have brought him because there was no one at home to look after him.
"This is ludicrous and never any parents' option to begin with," he said.
Saravanan also questioned MACC's position that the law imposed no age limit on such a notice.
He cited Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009, which provides for a person to furnish a statement on oath, with failure to comply carrying criminal consequences.
However, he said the legal system recognised that children might not have the capacity to understand the significance of an oath.
He cited Section 133A of the Evidence Act 1950, which provides for children of tender years to give unsworn evidence.
"So the question cannot simply be whether Section 36 contains the words '18' or '12'.
"It must also be whether applying an adult investigative mechanism to a 12-year-old produces an absurd and disproportionate result," he said.
Saravanan said Section 17A of the Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967 required legislation to be interpreted in a manner consistent with its purpose and effect.
He said the issue was not merely whether the law technically allowed such a notice, but whether the process was appropriate when applied to a child.
On Sept 25, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman
announced that asset declaration notices
would be served on Saravanan, his wife and 3 children on Sept 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-China ties must continue to be strengthened, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's long-standing diplomatic ties with China must continue to be strengthened based on the principles of mutual respect and shared benefits, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The deputy prime minister also expressed hope that close ties between Malaysia and China would continue to grow for the benefit of both countries and their people.
"Today, I received a farewell courtesy call from Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, who will be completing his tenure in the country.
"Throughout his tenure in Malaysia, many experiences, achievements and memories have undoubtedly been created together.
"I expressed my appreciation for Ouyang's commitment to strengthening ties between Malaysia and China, as well as his efforts to enhance cooperation between the governments, business sectors and people of both countries," he said in a post on his Facebook account today.
Zahid said they also exchanged views on the continued development of Malaysia-China relations and areas of cooperation that could be explored in the future.
"Thank you, Ouyang, for all your service and friendship during your time in Malaysia.
"I pray that he will continue to achieve success in whatever responsibilities he undertakes in the future," he said.

Title: JAC to assemble T9 pickups locally
Article:
EVOLELECTRIC Motors Sdn Bhd, the Malaysian distributor of JAC pickup trucks, has partnered with FT Assembly Sdn Bhd (FTA), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Feytech Holdings Bhd, to locally assemble JAC's T9 range in the country.
The phased completely knocked-down (CKD) programme will cover the T9 petrol plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), diesel and battery electric vehicle (BEV) variants.
The T9 PHEV will lead the programme, followed by the diesel and BEV versions, with production scheduled to start in November 2026.
Initial annual capacity is estimated at 3,000 units.
FTA has invested RM3.6 million to establish the JAC assembly facility at Feytech's manufacturing plant in Kulim, Kedah, with total investment potentially reaching RM8 million over the next three years.
The 84,000 sq ft facility includes vehicle assembly, inspection, testing and quality-control operations.
The CKD programme targets local content of up to 30 per cent.
It is expected to generate about RM230 million in annual economic value and will create jobs while supporting the local automotive supply chain.
The locally assembled T9 PHEV and BEV are expected to be the first locally assembled PHEV and BEV pickup trucks in Malaysia.
This will extend the country's vehicle assembly capabilities into the light commercial new energy vehicle segment.
Evolvelectric Motors chief executive officer Lau Yit Mun said the programme would strengthen JAC's long-term presence in Malaysia.
"JAC Pickup together with Evolvelectric Motors is building a stronger foundation in Malaysia by producing its pickup trucks locally," he said.
JAC is also exploring potential exports of pickups from Malaysia, subject to market conditions.
The T9 PHEV, which will be introduced as a completely built-up model in early November, offers a combined range of up to 1,000km and up to 1,000Nm of torque from its dual-motor system.
It also carries a five-star ANCAP safety rating.
The locally assembled T9 PHEV is expected to roll out in November 2026, while the BEV is targeted for January 2027.

Title: Syed Saddiq: 'Don't splurge for a day and end up in debt for decades'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Do not squander your savings just to splurge for a day and end up saddled with debt for decades," says Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman when asked about the budget for his upcoming wedding to artiste Bella Astillah.
Syed Saddiq, 33, said he was taking a serious approach to managing his finances, citing financial issues as a common cause of divorce.
"I discussed this with my future wife; we want to do our best because we want to send a positive message. I am someone who speaks based on data, so I view this matter seriously," he said at a press conference here this afternoon to announce their wedding.
The couple will hold two large-scale receptions in their home states — Johor and Sabah — with the public invited.
They will also organise a smaller reception here for close friends and fans, apart from their intimate nikah ceremony at Merdeka 118 Tower on Oct 10.
"I apologise to those who are left out from some of the planned events.
"Fortunately, media outlets like Astro are providing live coverage, so those unable to attend can still watch on television or online.
"But you're all still invited to join in the 'kenduri rakyat' in Muar and Kota Kinabalu," he said.
Bella said they were collaborating with several brands to provide doorgifts to the first 10,000 guests at both kenduri events.
The doorgifts will include 10,000kg of rice, coconut milk and instant ketupat, with an estimated total value of at least RM300,000.
"Rather than asking for cash (from sponsors), it is better to alleviate the public's burden while celebrating this joyous occasion together," said Syed Saddiq.

Title: Medical assistant drowns while swimming at Chemerong Waterfall
Article:
DUNGUN: A 25-year-old medical assistant drowned while swimming at Chemerong Waterfall here today.
Al-Muktafi Billah Shah Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Kama Suhaimi Abdullah said the victim, Mohd Ikmal Awid, who was stationed at Kemaman Hospital, was found at the scene at noon.
He said the department received a report on the incident at 11.46am, but firefighters who arrived at the scene found that the victim, from Kota Belud, Sabah, had already been located by his friends.
"The victim was said to be swimming with six of his friends when suddenly he and another friend were swept away by strong currents," he said in a statement.
Suhaimi said the victim's friend was rescued by their friends, but the victim could not be saved.
"About 15 minutes later, his friends made another dive and found the victim at noon," he said.
He said the victim was pronounced dead by a Health Ministry medical officer before his body was handed over to the police for further action.

Title: Two transporters arrested, 58.1kg ganja seized in Maran
Article:
KUANTAN: Two men were arrested after 56 compressed bricks of ganja weighing 58.1kg and worth RM174,000 were seized in Maran on Monday.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the suspects, aged 44 and 30, were detained around 1.20am while allegedly transferring four bags from the boot of a car in front of a homestay.
He said checks on the bags found 56 transparent plastic wrappers and aluminium foil containing dried compressed lumps suspected to be ganja.
"The current market value of the seized ganja is estimated at RM174,000 based on the price of RM3,000 per kilogramme," he told a press conference at the Pahang police headquarters here.
Azry Akmar said investigations found that the syndicate's modus operandi was to deliver drug supplies to areas where there was demand.
He said both suspects, believed to be from a northern state, admitted receiving RM10,000 to deliver the drugs to Maran.
"It is understood that this is the first time the group from the north carried out a delivery to the East Coast, specifically Pahang, as they previously operated mostly in the Klang Valley," he said.
He said background checks found that both men had previous drug-related records.
He added that the suspects had been remanded for seven days, from Monday to Sunday, to facilitate investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act.
The case is also being investigated under Section 15(1)(a) of the same Act after preliminary urine tests on both suspects returned positive for methamphetamine, he said.
Meanwhile, Azry Akmar said Ops Hawk, conducted statewide across Pahang over three days from Monday, led to the arrest of 365 individuals.
He said the arrests comprised 79 for drug supply offences, 90 for drug possession, 191 for urine-related offences and five under special preventive measures.
Drug seizures worth RM221,190 were also recorded during the operation.

Title: RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group.
In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures.
For the first eight months of the year, inflation averaged 1.8 per cent, alongside the restoration of the BUDI95 monthly quota and an increase in the diesel subsidy quota from September.
"For the rest of 2026, the inflation trajectory will be shaped by global commodity price movements, changes in domestic policies, as well as potential upside from food inflation," he said.
Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidy, stable food prices, stable demand conditions and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices should help keep inflation contained.
Meanwhile, he said the overnight policy rate is expected to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the upcoming November Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting amid manageable inflation.
Moving forward, Gan said RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures.
He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure.
At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026.
"The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account.
"Together, these should sustain Malaysia's current account surplus," added Gan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign man feared buried in Lojing Highlands landslide
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A foreign man is feared buried in a landslide at workers' quarters on a vegetable farm in the Lojing Highlands here today.
Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station chief Muhammad Azrul Izzham Zulkifli said the department received a distress call at 4.12pm, with a team arriving at the scene, about 92km away, at 5.30pm.
"There was a landslide involving a slope about 50m high," he said when contacted today.
Azrul said a search and rescue operation for the man began at 5.54pm, with assistance from the police.

Title: Existing taxes key to 2027 Budget, expect few major changes: Expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh.
He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts.
Speaking at a forum hosted by CIMB Securities, Veerinderjeet said the government should "sweat our assets".
This is by improving collection efficiency, with scope to gradually raise Malaysia's tax-to-gross domestic product ratio towards 15 per cent through stronger personal, corporate and indirect tax bases.
He expects few major tax changes in the upcoming budget, given the continued focus on cost-of-living support and social spending.
Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget.
A further increase in the 30 per cent top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely.
On the sales and service tax (SST), Veerinderjeet estimates coverage has reached about 78-80 per cent of goods and services, bringing it closer to the breadth of the former goods and services tax (GST).
He sees scope for broader input exemptions under SST to reduce cascading effects and business costs, although this would mean some revenue loss.
GST reinstatement is not expected in thr 2027 Budget, with improving SST efficiency likely to take precedence.
Wider e-invoicing participation could also help uncover unreported taxable activity, although exemptions for smaller businesses may be gradually reduced as economic conditions improve.
On other measures, Veerinderjeet expects limited additional revenue from the global minimum tax until the first filing cycle provides clearer evidence of collections.
A carbon tax remains on the policy agenda but could be delayed to 2028 or later amid business cost pressures.
The budget may reaffirm the government's intention to introduce it, potentially at a low initial rate.
He also sees only a slight possibility of modest excise duty increases on alcohol and tobacco, while no new windfall levy is expected.
For real estate investment trusts, he does not expect the former 10 per cent final withholding tax on distributions to return, although he supports withholding mechanisms to reduce filing and monitoring costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Marriage isn't just about love' — Siti Hasmah's advice to Syed Saddiq, Bella
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and artiste Bella Astillah said the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali was cheerful and in high spirits when they last met her, three days before her death.
Syed Saddiq said there was nothing unusual about the former prime minister's wife during their final meeting, which lasted more than two hours, and that she had even shared how much she was looking forward to attending their wedding.
He said the meeting would remain one of their most cherished memories.
"During that meeting, she was in very high spirits," he said when met at a press conference on their upcoming wedding here this afternoon.
Syed Saddiq said Siti Hasmah also offered advice on married life, particularly on the importance of compromise and tolerance between partners.
"She shared a lot of advice, especially on the importance of compromise in a marriage.
"Marriage is not merely about love; it is about tolerance, the wisdom to compromise, weathering trials together and managing issues such as jealousy within the relationship," he said.
Syed Saddiq said Siti Hasmah remained cheerful throughout the meeting, sharing jokes and reminiscing about events from decades ago, including her romance with former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
"She was still able to joke and recall events from 50 or 60 years ago, including her love story with Dr Mahathir," he said.
Meanwhile, Bella said Siti Hasmah had advised her to be a strong woman, stand by her husband's side and maintain a gentle nature in navigating married life.
"There are things I can share and others I choose to keep private out of respect for her. She told me that the journey of being a politician's wife is not an easy one.
"However, as long as there is trust in the relationship, God willing, the marriage will endure. Tolerance and mutual respect for one's partner are also crucial," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar congratulates athletes as Malaysia add three more Asian Games golds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes after the national contingent secured three more gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan today.
Anwar said the achievement was a source of pride and highlighted the athletes' exceptional ability and determination.
He said the feat brought Malaysia's gold medal tally to nine as the national contingent continued its campaign to fly the Jalur Gemilang high on the Asian stage.
"Congratulations and well done to all the gold medal winners today," he said in a Facebook post.
The three gold medals were won by track cycling ace Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang in the men's keirin at the Izu Velodrome, while Malaysia also claimed gold in both the women's and men's squash team events at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena.
In the women's final, Aifa Azman, S. Sivasangari, Aira Azman and Rachel Arnold defeated Hong Kong 2-1.
The men's team, comprising Ng Eain Yow, Sanjay Jeeva, C. Ameeshenraj and Mohammad Syafiq Kamal, defeated Pakistan 2-0.
Anwar also called on Malaysians to continue praying for the national athletes competing in tomorrow's finals.
"Tomorrow, the fight for gold continues, with the men's padel pair Christian Didier Chin and Aidan Yunus, as well as the men's hockey squad, competing in the finals. Let us pray together for their success," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Embraer supply chain: Defence Ministry explores aerospace deal amid RMAF C-390 talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is exploring opportunities to participate in Brazilian aerospace and defence company Embraer's regional and global supply chain as part of efforts to strengthen the local defence industry.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said this followed a courtesy visit by Embraer Defence and Security chief commercial officer Frederico Lemos at Wisma Pertahanan today.
"The meeting provided an opportunity to explore cooperation in developing the local downstream ecosystem, including opportunities for Malaysia to participate in Embraer's supply chain at the regional and global levels.
"This potential is in line with the aspirations of the National Defence Industry Policy (DIPN) to strengthen the capabilities of the local defence industry," he said in a Facebook post.
Embraer is a Brazilian aerospace and defence company specialising in aircraft development and integrated defence solutions.
The New Straits Times
previously reported
that Embraer's C-390 was among the aircraft being considered as a potential replacement for the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) ageing C-130 Hercules fleet.
RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris had said the successor should have a similar carrying capacity to the Hercules and meet Malaysia's operational requirements.
"The eventual successor to the C-130 should have a similar carrying capacity. We know that is the capacity we need most of the time. Not too big and not too small. Just the right size," Norazlan said.
The C-390 can carry up to 26 tonnes of cargo and about 80 soldiers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farm Price declares maiden dividend since May 2024 listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Farm Price Holdings Bhd - a Johor-based wholesaler and distributor of fresh vegetables, food and beverage products and groceries - has declared its first dividend since listing on Bursa Malaysia in May 2024.
The company announced a single-tier interim dividend of 0.6 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, involving a total payout of about RM2.7 million.
The dividend will be paid on Nov 11 to shareholders registered as at Oct 19.
Managing director Dr Lawrence Tiong Lee Chian said the maiden dividend reflected the group's confidence in its financial performance and cash flow position.
"This also demonstrates the financial discipline we have maintained in our operations, and we intend to continue rewarding our shareholders with regular dividends in the future, subject to the Group's cash flow position and capital requirements," he said.
Separately, Farm Price secured approvals to expand its Senai Centralised Distribution Centre by about 71,000 square feet, bringing total built-up area to about 150,000 sq ft.
Fit-out work is under way, with full operations targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
The expanded facility, including about 67,000 sq ft of cold-room space, will cater to growing demand in Malaysia and Singapore and boost its capacity for pre-packed and ready-to-cook vegetables.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amazon to invest US$1bil over five years in US data center communities
Article:
WASHINGTON: Amazon's cloud computing division said on Friday it would invest more than US$1 billion over the next five years in US communities where it has data centers and vowed to tackle their impacts on electricity and water usage.
Data centers, which provide the computing power ​to train and run AI models, have drawn opposition in communities nationwide over concerns about electricity demand, utility costs and other local impacts. The ⁠backlash poses a political challenge for Republicans heading into the US midterm elections on November 3.
Amazon said it had invested US$276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025 and had large projects or expansions in the works in many states including Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia and Mississippi.
Amazon Web Services said the community investment plans announced on Friday would include spending on education, job training, energy affordability, water and energy preservation and other local priorities in parts of the US where it has data centers.
The company in a lengthy statement sought to rebut criticism of data centers tied to environmental, energy and economic impacts and noted there were more than 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country.
"There is urgency to this data center buildout because we aren't the only country that sees the benefits of AI for the economy and national security, and the countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it," AWS CEO Matt Garman said.
AWS also committed to being water positive across its data centers by 2030 by returning more water to communities than it uses and said it was 75 per cent of the way toward its goal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: iSHAR 2026 focuses on regional Shariah challenges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Rakyat is strengthening discussions on the future of Islamic finance through the 2026 International Shariah Scholars Roundtable (iSHAR), in collaboration with the Association of Shariah Advisors in Islamic Finance.
Entering its sixth edition, iSHAR 2026 features a regional edition for the first time, focusing on shared Shariah, governance and operational issues among Southeast Asian countries.
Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Mohd Irwan Mohd Mubarak said Shariah research and knowledge development must be grounded in operational realities and evolving economic needs.
"We need research grounded in operational realities, innovation that preserves the objectives of Shariah, and human capital capable of bridging an understanding of Islamic law with current economic needs," he said in a statement.
He said collaboration among financial institutions, regulators, fatwa institutions, academia and industry experts was important to develop relevant and practical Shariah solutions.
The two-day conference, held on Oct 1-2,  brought together about 180 participants, including 43 Shariah scholars, as well as representatives from regulators and financial institutions in Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.
Key issues discussed included Shariah non-compliance in Tawarruq, Ijarah, Musharakah and Mudharabah, cash waqf and Ar-Rahnu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No more bets: 46 nabbed in KL gambling call centre raids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested 46 foreigners in raids on nine suspected online gambling call centres across the capital over the past two days.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the raids were carried out under Op Dadu Khas on Oct 1 and 2.
"The foreigners are suspected of operating online gambling call centres and are also being investigated for immigration offences.
"Initial investigations found that all those arrested admitted to being involved in organising online gambling activities targeting customers from China, Korea and the Philippines," he said in a statement.
He said the operations are believed to have been active for between one and three months, with those involved receiving monthly salaries of between RM2,000 and RM3,500.
Fadil said police seized RM23,000 in cash along with equipment allegedly used in the operations.
"The items included 24 laptop computers, 71 mobile phones, 10 WiFi modems, 12 monitors, three access cards, a router, four other laptops, three keyboards, five chargers, five computer mice and three sets of keys.
"The cases are being investigated under Sections 4(1)(g) and 4B(a) of the Common Gaming Houses Act 1953, as well as Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63," he said adding that all 46 suspects were brought before a magistrate for remand applications.
He said 11 of them were remanded for three days from Oct 1 to Oct 3, one was remanded for a day until Oct 2, while another 22 were remanded for four days from Oct 2 to Oct 5.
"The remaining 12 have been remanded for 14 days from Oct 1 to Oct 15 to facilitate investigations.
"We advise the public to stay away from all forms of gambling and remain vigilant against scams using call centre operations as their modus operandi," he said.
Those with information on gambling or fraudulent activities can contact the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999 or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chery adds sporty twist to Tiggo Cross
Article:
CHERY Malaysia is expanding its Tiggo Cross line-up with the upcoming Tiggo Cross Sport Edition, adding a sportier exterior treatment to its compact SUV range.
The new variant gets revised front and rear lips designed to give the SUV a more aggressive stance, with Chery positioning the model towards younger motorists and sports enthusiasts.
The Tiggo Cross Sport Edition will initially be offered exclusively with the Turbo powertrain, with full specifications, pricing and other details to be announced at its launch next month.
The model forms part of Chery Malaysia's wider push into sports and e-sports.
The company recently supported the Lee Chong Wei Cup badminton tournament and is the official mobility partner of the KL Women Running Festival.
It is also the official automotive partner of the Mobile Legends: Bang Bang Professional League (MPL) Malaysia Season 18.
As part of the partnership, Chery said the Season 18 Legenda prize, coinciding with the 10th anniversary of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, will be upgraded to a Tiggo Cross Sport Edition.
Chery has previously linked its brand activities to sports through support for athletes, including Olympians and Paralympians.
The Sport Edition brings that theme to the vehicle itself, with the added exterior elements intended to distinguish it from the standard Tiggo Cross.
More details on the new variant will be released closer to its launch this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Senior citizen held at gunpoint, RM23,000 jewellery stolen
Article:
GURUN: A 67-year-old woman was threatened with a pistol by a man who broke into her house at Taman Seri Jerai 2 here yesterday before fleeing with RM23,000 worth of jewellery.
Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the victim was alone at home when the incident occurred around 9.20am.
He said the suspect entered the house and pointed the pistol at the victim.
"The suspect then snatched the gold necklace and two gold bracelets worn by the victim.
"He fled in a red car of an unknown make and model," he said in a statement.
Hanyan said the victim suffered bruises on both wrists.
The victim had lodged a report at the Gurun police station.
Following investigations, officers from the Kedah Criminal Investigation Department's Special Investigation Division (D9) together with the Kuala Muda CID arrested the suspect around 11.15pm yesterday.
He said the 41-year-old suspect was arrested at a house in Taman Permai Utama here.
"Investigations found that only one suspect was involved in the incident. The suspect had also conducted surveillance on the victim's house for two weeks before the incident.
"On the day of the incident, the suspect entered the house after seeing the victim's husband leave and being convinced that she was alone," he said.
Hanyan said the suspect had no previous criminal record and the case was being investigated under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Berjaya Hills Resort seeks Federal Court leave over RM25.75mil quit rent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd (BHRB) is seeking leave from the Federal Court to appeal against a decision upholding the Pahang government's revision of its quit rent, with the application set to be heard on Dec 8.
In a statement today, BHRB said it filed the application on Aug 14 after the Court of Appeal on July 16 upheld the Temerloh High Court's dismissal of its challenge against the revised quit rent rates.
The company said the development came as the Pahang state authorities began enforcement action against its properties at Berjaya Hills on Sept 28, including staff quarters, a central laundry and other essential facilities.
BHRB described the enforcement action as "unconscionable and totally unacceptable", saying it was unreasonable and extreme given that its application for leave to appeal remained pending.
"Whilst BHRB respects the decisions of the High Court and the Court of Appeal concerning the state government's revision of quit rent rates, the company is deeply disappointed and saddened by the courts' decision," it said.
The dispute began in 2020 when BHRB said its annual quit rent was increased from about RM2.4 million in 2019 to RM33.7 million, a 13-fold increase.
The company said it subsequently lodged 11 appeals with the Pahang government between April 2020 and December 2022, following which the annual quit rent was reduced to RM25.75 million.
BHRB said it had paid about RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties between 2020 and 2026 while continuing to seek a further review of the rate.
"BHRB had no choice but to make quit rent payments under protest between 2020 and 2026, and paid approximately RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties," it said.
The company subsequently filed judicial review proceedings at the Temerloh High Court in April 2023, challenging the revised quit rent rate.
The High Court dismissed the application on May 29, 2024, ruling that it could not intervene in the state government's policy decision on the revision of quit rent rates.
BHRB said the substantial increase in quit rent and subsequent enforcement action were "unreasonable" and "unconscionable", and could affect future local and foreign investment in Pahang.
The company said it remained hopeful of a positive outcome from its legal action and hoped the Pahang government would continue engaging with it towards a "mutually acceptable and amicable resolution".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Season Optical earns dual recognition from Asean, Asia Records
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Season Optical received dual recognition from Asean Records and Asia Records after selling 1,111 pairs of eyewear during a three-day warehouse sale at U Sentral, Masai, from Sept 25 to 27.
The record was officially certified on Sept 27 under the category, "First Mart-Based Eyewear Chain to Surpass 1,000 Pairs Sold in a Three-Day Warehouse Sale with a Live Public Sales Tally".
The sales tally was displayed publicly in real time throughout the event.
Access to vision care
Founded in 2015, Season Optical offers eyewear at different price points, with access to suitable products influenced by factors including cost.
Its focus includes improving access to eyewear and related services for families and children who may face barriers to obtaining them.
The company said clear vision could affect learning and development among children, as well as work and daily activities for adults.
Season Optical offers eyewear packages starting from RM28, alongside established brands and higher-priced products.
It has also expanded from Johor to other parts of Malaysia over the years.
Community vision care
Season Optical's activities include corporate social responsibility (CSR) and community programmes involving children and groups that may face difficulties accessing eyewear and vision care.
The company has partnered with Yayasan Sultan Ibrahim Johor (YSIJ) on initiatives involving students and communities in Johor, including providing eyewear to students in need.
Season Optical co-founder Sally Loh said the milestone reflected the support the company had received from customers and the local community.
"For us, 1,111 pairs of eyewear is not merely a sales figure.
"This record belongs to Season Optical, but it also belongs to our customers, the community and the people of Johor who have supported us throughout our journey," she said.
Loh said the company hoped its activities would contribute to wider access to eyewear and vision care.
"We started from Johor with the belief that good vision should not become a choice reserved for a select few because of price.
"We hope this record will help more people discover Season Optical, while enabling more Malaysians to access quality eyewear and vision care at reasonable prices," she said.
Marking a new milestone
The achievement was celebrated at a closing ceremony on Sept 27, attended by Marsai Jaya Elektrik Sdn Bhd director Gan Cheng Swee and Datuk Fazley Yaakob.
The company said it plans to expand its business and service network across Malaysia while continuing its community vision care initiatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tan Chong, SAIC-GM-Wuling to start EV battery localisation
Article:
TAN Chong Motor Group and SAIC-GM-Wuling (SGMW) are stepping up efforts to localise electric vehicle (EV) battery production in Malaysia.
The efforts will start with the assembly of batteries under the TQ Wuling brand.
The companies signed a cooperation agreement at the 23rd China-Asean Expo (Caexpo) in Nanning, Guangxi, on Sept 17, covering the localisation and completely knocked-down (CKD) assembly of EV batteries.
The agreement was signed by Liu Zhijun, director of marketing and service at Liuzhou Saike Technology, SGMW, and Wan Wei Sun, head of TQ Wuling, on behalf of Tan Chong.
The move is among the first major initiatives under SGMW's newly announced Global 5 Strategy.
It seeks to expand the Chinese automaker's international operations beyond vehicle exports into manufacturing, supply chains, sales, talent and financial capabilities.
The partnership will focus initially on building a more localised EV battery supply chain in Malaysia, while supporting SGMW's broader production and supply-chain integration across Asean.
The battery localisation programme builds on the existing partnership between Tan Chong and SGMW through TQ Wuling.
The companies said localising core EV components would help develop Malaysia's new energy vehicle supply chain and deepen SGMW's industrial presence in Malaysia and the wider Asean region.
It also aims to facilitate greater cross-border industrial cooperation between China, Malaysia and Asean.
SGMW's Global 5 Strategy was launched at Caexpo under the theme "Global Wuling, Shining Across Asean".
The strategy is built around five key strengths — its product portfolio, "Tian-Ling-Shen" technology system, Intelligent Island Manufacturing System (I²MS), five-chain industrial ecosystem and 68 years of automotive manufacturing experience.
SGMW has produced and sold more than 32 million vehicles globally, including more than four million new energy vehicles.
Its overseas exports have grown for 10 consecutive years, with cumulative exports exceeding 1.6 million vehicles and vehicle sets.
SGMW said Asean is a strategic gateway for its global expansion, with Malaysia serving as an important market for developing local industrial capabilities.
Its international cooperation models range from vehicle trade and distribution to local production, full industrial-chain cooperation and technology licensing.
The company said the partnership with Tan Chong combines SGMW's EV technology and manufacturing capabilities with the Malaysian group's established automotive presence and local market experience.
Both sides will continue to explore further localisation opportunities as they seek to expand Malaysia's role in SGMW's growing Asean and global automotive ecosystem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Samaiden bags 99.99MW solar contracts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Samaiden Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd has secured contracts for a 99.99 megawatt alternating current large-scale solar photovoltaic plant.
The contracts from Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTLSB) cover engineering, construction and commissioning works, as well as the supply of solar components.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Samaiden said the contracts were entered into on Oct 2 for the development of the project under the Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) programme.
The project was among the LSS photovoltaic projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025 under the LSS5+ programme.
Samaiden said the scope includes the supply and delivery of materials, design, engineering, construction, testing and completion of the solar photovoltaic energy generating facility.
"Due to confidentiality restrictions in the contracts, the sum for the works cannot be disclosed," it said in the filing.
Works will commence upon the issuance of the notice to proceed in accordance with the terms of the contracts.
YTLSB, which is principally involved in construction, has been appointed the main contractor for the project.
Samaiden said the contracts are expected to contribute positively to the group's future earnings during the duration.
